description: I am, a 7th-grade student, building interactive 3D worlds in Minecraft and Tinkercad, designing in Blender, and programs in Python. Codementum Silver Medalist, AzeRobot Young Engineer (2026), WRO national participant (2025). On Team BHP1 I build a Minecraft museum for Abandoned but not Forgotten: a button opens the door and wakes up NASA retired rovers and probes.
summary: Forgotten Explorers is a learn-then-play Minecraft game for ages 10-14 about the hardware NASA has left behind on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space. At the entrance, players choose one retired explorer from a list taken from the challenge's Resources: for example Apollo Lunar Modules, Surveyor 3, Sojourner, Spirit and Opportunity, Viking, Pioneer 10 and 11. Each explorer's world has three levels. A level starts with real NASA images and a short story. Then the player rides a minecart until a door blocks the way, and a question must be answered to open it. Our prototype has the hub and a playable world for Opportunity: its airbag landing, the signs of past water and the dust storm that ended contact. Every other explorer will use the same template, so the game can grow to cover all of NASA's retired hardware.
details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS
The game is designed as a hub of worlds: the player picks a retired NASA explorer from a list, then plays three levels. In this prototype the hub shows several explorers, and we built one world, Opportunity. More worlds will be added in the full game. Each level has three steps: (1) real NASA images and a short fact card, (2) a Minecraft scene, (3) a question. The player rides a minecart along a corridor, a door blocks the way, and pressing the correct button opens it. Level 1 is the airbag landing, Level 2 is the “blueberries” and signs of water, Level 3 is the 2018 dust storm. Other explorers will use the same template: only the story, NASA images and questions change.

BENEFITS
Kids see real NASA visuals first and then recall them to open the next door, which makes the facts easier to remember. Each level links engineering to science: airbags and a safe landing, arm instruments and clues about water, solar panels and power.

INTENDED IMPACT
We want retired missions to feel as exciting to kids as active ones, and to let kids meet many NASA explorers, not just one.

TOOLS
Minecraft (minecarts, redstone doors), PowerPoint (slides), OBS (screen recording), CapCut (video editing). AI tools: Claude AI and Grok AI (see the AI use section below).

CREATIVITY
The quiz becomes movement: you must answer to keep moving. The hub lets a child choose a favorite explorer, and one template makes new worlds quick to add.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED
Accessibility: English subtitles, short texts, high-contrast slides, and a game kids already know. Cost: free or low-cost tools and free NASA images. Energy: runs on an ordinary computer.

AI USE
We used Claude AI and Grok AI to search for and collect information from NASA pages and to help plan and edit our English texts. Claude AI also produced a first draft of the PowerPoint prototype. We then edited the slides ourselves and replaced the AI-generated pictures with our own. One picture (the final image) is AI-generated by Claude; it is labeled “AI-generated” under the image in the slides and in the video. The team checked the facts against NASA pages, built the Minecraft world level by level, and recorded and edited the video ourselves.
